title: Catalog entry metadata contract and compatibility tokenization for new open models
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: When ingesting community/open model weights we lack a concise, machine-readable metadata contract and a compact compatibility token set that runtime and routing teams can rely on. Current free-form notes cause repeated runtime surprises (failed kernels, KV cache misses, quantization-incompatibility) and inconsistent pinning decisions. Goal: Define a lightweight metadata contract (fields + value enum) and a small set of compatibility tokens that capture runtime-relevant properties. This ticket scopes the product-level requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout constraints for the metadata contract. Scope in: schema fields, required vs optional annotations, human-readable summary, compatibility token definitions (kernel, kvcache, quant, io-shape), mapping to onboarding lifecycle states (probe, vet, certify, retire), API surface for catalog entries, and documentation templates for model submitters. Scope out: implementation details for runtime enforcement, SDK changes, and infra migrations (these will be owned by ENG tasks). Tradeoffs considered: longer schema vs adoption friction (we opt for compact tokens + extensible free-form notes), mandatory signals vs slower intake (start with a small required set), and hard version locks vs soft advisory flags (prefer advisory soft-lock with clear rollback triggers).
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable JSON schema is published that includes: model_id, source_url, semantic_version, compat_tokens, recommended_runtime_profile, sample_input_shapes, and human_summary

Compat tokens defined and limited to at most 6 primary tokens: KRN (kernel_compat), KVC (kv_cache_safe), QNT (quant_support), STR (sequence_length_profile), TPU (accelerator_restrictions), IOF (io_format), each with a documented enum and example values
Onboarding lifecycle states documented with transition rules: probe -> vet -> certify -> GA -> deprecate/retire, including duration guidance and automated probe checks
A 10-case runtime probe checklist (artifact links included) that ENG can run automatically during 'probe' including kernel load, kv cache warmup, quant-inference sanity, and throughput baseline
API contract for catalog entries (fields and types) merged into the public PRD and example POST/PUT payloads provided for submitters
Two example community model submissions updated to include the new metadata format (links provided) and validated by QA harness
Rollout plan with gating: soft-adopt for 2 weeks (accept both old and new metadata), then optional enforcement for new submissions, with rollback steps and monitoring dash included
